        DEFORM / LINEAR BLEND

        Skinning & weights

        WEIGHT TRANSFER · BODY → GARMENT

        Each garment vertex copies the joint influences at the closest point on the body surface (up to four, renormalized). Vertices past the max distance fall back to the nearest joint segments and are reported. Like Bind, a transfer clears undo history.

        BATCH · GARMENTS × BODIES

        Pick at least one garment and one body to queue a task.

        Every garment × body pair runs on its own: over-limit garments and unprepared bodies are skipped with a reason, and one failed pair never stops the rest. Bind-class work clears undo history, so undo ends up cleared after a batch.

        MULTI-GARMENT AUTO-RIG
        Garment GLBs

        CLOTH · PREVIEW (EXPERIMENTAL)

        Preview-quality XPBD simulation: distance and bending constraints, gravity, damping, bone-capsule collisions, and a soft attachment that keeps strongly weighted vertices on their skinned pose. Deterministic from frame 0 — the same start state always produces the same result. Baking writes the simulated shape into the bind geometry (bind-class operation, clears undo). Cloth keeps its own limit: garments up to 30,000 triangles and 30,000 vertices, independent of the larger skinning limit. Stop and report if a heavy mesh runs slow or falls apart.

        SIZES · GARMENT VARIANTS

        Up to ten pre-draped garment GLBs per set — one per body size. Switching hides the current variant, shows the chosen one and carries the placement over; an incoming size that was never bound is bound to the same skeleton and pulls the body's weights across by nearest surface, so it follows the skeleton immediately. Joint keys, poses and the timeline are untouched, and each variant keeps its own object keys. Sets persist in saved projects.

        FIT · PLACEMENT

        Position the garment against the body with numeric move, rotate and scale fields, optional snapping and a live overlap warning. Copy placement exports the transform as nine plain numbers.

        POSE TEST · GARMENT FIT

        Four built-in stress poses (arms down, arms up, elbow bend, shoulder twist) plus every compatible pose-library pose run one at a time on top of your exact starting pose, which is restored afterwards. Edges compressed below 60% of rest length count as pinched; vertices pushed inside the body surface count as clipped. The worst pose stays highlighted in the viewport so the weight brush knows where to work.

        Stop freezes the displayed playhead and reapplies its exact sampled pose; use Jump to start to rewind. Drag the ruler or an empty track area to scrub; playback pauses while you edit. Duration is 1–120 whole seconds, at 12, 24, 30 or 60 fps. Changing FPS preserves time, rounded to the nearest new frame. Shortening duration clamps the playhead. Frames are zero-based: the end boundary equals duration × FPS, and loops wrap without an extra frame. Space works from the viewport and buttons; typing fields and dialogs retain their normal keyboard behavior. Playback pauses when this tab is hidden. Timing follows a monotonic clock, without cumulative frame-step drift. Evaluation commits all local transforms and world matrices before publishing each frame. A busy device skips overdue visual samples instead of slowing the clock; Engine timing reports those skips honestly. For seamless loops, author matching first and last poses. Performance view uses native-pixel rendering and stable selection bounds; detailed silhouette outlines are optional in Engine timing. CPU timings do not certify GPU/display presentation or any particular hardware. Authored transform keys drive playback; embedded glTF clips are retained but not mixed into these tracks. Keys hold their first/last value outside their interval. Rotation interpolates local Euler components with segment easing, preserving full turns. Edit the selected object in the Transform panel, then press K outside typing fields (or click Key all). Drag a diamond to retime only that key; occupied times are rejected. Delete removes the selected diamond. Scroll the track list to reach other objects, or select an object in the hierarchy to reveal its tracks. Large scenes virtualize offscreen track rows without removing any animation data. Keys retain their time in seconds when FPS changes, and out-of-range keys are kept when duration shrinks. Undo/redo covers transform and keyframe edits; removing a model clears this edit history. Save project downloads a .motionlab file containing original models, textures, edited transforms, keys, timeline and view. Open project restores it offline; saving pauses playback. Embedded project assets are limited to 128 MB.

        WESTWILDD FIT

        Weight transfer dresses a garment with a body's weights: open Skinning, bind the body mesh to its skeleton, then in Weight transfer pick the body as source and the garment as target. Every garment vertex copies the joint influences at the closest point on the body surface — up to four, renormalized — so the garment follows the same skeleton as the body. A max surface distance excludes far-away parts; vertices without a match fall back to the nearest joint segments and are counted in the report. The result behaves like any other bound mesh: the weight heat view works on it, it survives project save/load and it exports with animated GLB. Transfer is a binding-class operation and clears undo history, like Bind.

        Batch bind queues whole sets: open Skinning and use Batch · garments × bodies to multi-select garments and bodies, pick Transfer weights or Automatic weights, then run the queue. Each pair reports its own outcome — OK with vertex counts, SKIPPED with a reason when the garment is over the 250,000-triangle hard limit — skinning itself is tuned up to 150,000 triangles and 100,000 vertices per mesh — or the body has no weights to transfer yet, FAILED with the error if a pair breaks mid-run — and one bad pair never stops the rest. Automatic weights can also dress a body that was never bound itself, as long as its model carries an imported skeleton. Bind-class work clears undo history, so undo ends up cleared when the batch finishes.

        Weight paint edits joint weights directly: bind a mesh, open Skinning and press Paint weights. Left-drag paints on the deformed garment (right-drag orbits); pick the joint, then Add, Subtract or Smooth, set radius and strength, and enable Mirror across the garment's local X = 0 plane to work both sides at once — the mirrored stroke uses the matching _L/_R, .L/.R or Left/Right joint when one exists, and the same joint otherwise. Weights stay normalized with at most four influences per vertex, the heat view follows every stroke, each stroke can be undone while the brush is open, and painted weights survive project save/load and export with the animated GLB. Finishing the brush clears undo history, like Bind.

        Pose test checks how weights hold up under motion: open Skinning and use Pose test · garment fit to pick a bound garment and a bound body surface, then run. Four built-in stress poses — arms down, arms up, elbow bend, shoulder twist — plus every compatible pose-library pose run one at a time on top of your exact starting pose, which is restored bit-for-bit afterwards. A pose reports how many garment edges were compressed below 60% of their rest length (pinched, shown orange) and how many garment vertices ended up inside the body surface (clipped, shown red, with the deepest penetration). One skipped pose never stops the rest. The worst pose stays highlighted in the viewport after the run, so you know exactly where to take the weight brush — smooth the highlighted area and run the test again to watch the counts drop.

        Fit view places the garment: open Skinning and press Open fit view, or work entirely from the floating panel. Nine numeric fields move, rotate and scale the garment (rotation in degrees; scale is a relative factor — 1.00 keeps the current size, because garment nodes often carry a tiny imported scale that would make absolute values misleading); a snap setting quantizes every commit so nudges stay predictable. Auto-fit to body sizes the garment against the body's torso — matched on torso depth and shoulder-to-waist height so hanging arms do not skew it — and centres the scaled garment on that torso band, which lands the collar near the neck for jacket-like garments; fine-tune with the numeric fields afterwards. Any other mesh in the scene can serve as the body surface, bound or not. After each edit the garment is checked against the chosen body surface with a signed-distance test — vertices pushed inside the body turn red in the viewport and the panel reports how many and how deep, clearing themselves once the garment is out again. Copy placement puts nine plain numbers (position, rotation in degrees, scale) on the clipboard and in a read-only field for macro sheets. Placement edits ride the standard transform editor, so app-level Undo reverts them, and the fit view refuses to open over an active paint brush.

        Size sets keep whole wardrobes ready: import one pre-draped garment GLB per body size, open Skinning and use Sizes · garment variants to pick the base garment and multi-select the other sizes, then create the set (up to ten variants). Switching hides the current garment, shows the chosen size, carries the current placement over so nothing jumps, and — when the incoming size was never bound — binds it to the same skeleton and pulls the body's weights across by nearest surface, so it follows the animation immediately. Joint keys, the timeline and saved poses are untouched, and each variant keeps its own object keys. Size sets survive project save/load with their visibility and active variant, and variants whose model was removed are pruned from the set automatically.

        Cloth preview (experimental) drapes a bound garment with a lightweight XPBD simulation: distance and bending constraints, gravity, damping, bone-capsule collisions sized by a collision margin, and a soft attachment that keeps strongly weighted vertices on their skinned pose while loose cloth settles. The preview renders off a dynamic geometry swap and is deterministic from frame 0 — the same start state always produces the same drape. Bake to shape writes the simulated drape into the bind geometry (bind-class operation, clears undo), where it survives save/load and exports with the garment; Discard throws the preview away without touching anything. This is preview-quality cloth, not a production simulator. The preview keeps its own smaller limit — garments up to 30,000 triangles and 30,000 vertices, independent of the larger skinning limit — and refuses heavier garments with a clear message.

        INSTANT CYCLES

        Use the cycle toolbar button to create Loop, Ping-Pong, or Offset Loop from authored PRS keys. Offset Loop supports phase shifts, accumulating position/Euler deltas, or both. Seam blending is non-destructive. Convert back restores the original keys exactly; the separate frame bake is sampled. Creating a cycle turns off whole-take rewind, because a finite take may end mid-cycle and accumulating travel cannot return to its initial world position. Paths and secondary motion remain later layers.

        PATHS & TRAJECTORIES

        Open Paths to create 3D guides. Drag control spheres or edit local XYZ, then assign a path to any object or bone. Choose start/duration or progress keys, forward/up axes, orientation and banking. Key both path transform and shape in the studio. The ↔ controls retime keys without changing their values. Shape keys require fixed point count. Source PRS keys stay intact; projects save editable paths, and GLB bakes playback with editor metadata. Secondary motion runs after path following.

        SECONDARY MOTION

        Add per-object/bone Swing or Position lag layers from the spring toolbar icon. Amount, Frequency and Damping control deterministic follow-through; optional idle sway continues on stationary targets. Source keys are untouched, and muting immediately restores the authored result. Projects store settings; GLB bakes the result. The solver starts at frame zero and resets on each loop. Close the editor before measuring actual playback FPS. A 15-antenna demo is available in an empty scene.

        POSE LIBRARY

        Open Pose Library from the toolbar. Save named poses with folders and generated rig thumbnails. Root, bones and necessary parent controls are captured as local transforms. Compatible rigs must match unique bone names and their full hierarchy. Current-to-saved and saved-A-to-B blending use shortest-path quaternion rotations; previews add no keys. Apply writes Position, Rotation and Scale on every bone/root control at the playhead as one Undo operation. Close or Cancel restores previews. Libraries travel in format-8 projects and .motionposes files. No humanoid retargeting or IK/contact correction is performed.

        MOTION CURVES

        Double-click a Position, Rotation, Scale or Weight track (label, lane or key) to open its curve editor. Easing belongs to each left/outgoing key: Linear, Smooth, Sharp, Bounce, Elastic, Back or Custom Bezier. Drag a value-graph key to retime/change its selected component; double-click empty graph space to add a key. Bezier time handles are 0–1, progress handles −2–3. Blue handles drag live; morph playback is clamped to 0–100%. Curves use Undo/Redo and survive .motionlab save/load and recovery. GLB contains sampled curves plus editable metadata. Facial-owned curves must be detached before direct editing. A 25-curve demo is available from the Curves toolbar button in an empty workspace.

        EXPORT & RECOVERY

        The toolbar Export arrow writes animated GLB: meshes, skeletons, morphs and authored tracks, plus optional original imported clips. The authored take plays first in external viewers and restores editable keys when imported back into MotionLab. Euler turns are sampled adaptively; sparse morph buffers keep files compact. Retained keys beyond the visible timeline extend the exported take so no keys are discarded. Save a .motionlab file for full editor state, facial recipes and libraries. Browser Recovery, in the timeline footer, checkpoints every 60 seconds without pausing playback. Small checkpoints use localStorage; the two latest completed payloads use IndexedDB. Recovery found on launch waits for Restore or Continue; it never silently replaces the scene. Storage can be blocked in private or sandboxed contexts. Download portable files regularly.

        LIGHTWEIGHT JOINTS

        Create a root joint using the connected-circles button in the Objects header (or the empty-scene button). Select a joint and use the + child button to extend its chain along local +Y. The joint hierarchy and viewport spheres/links select each other; clicking a link selects its child. Rotate with the existing local Rotation fields, then press K or click Key all. Parent transforms propagate through every descendant. Eight levels are supported, with cycles and deeper branches rejected. Expand Joint settings to rename, change the parent, detach to scene root, or delete a joint and its descendants. Reparenting preserves LOCAL values and keys, not the world-space pose. Deleting a branch also deletes its keys. Topology/name edits clear the edit undo history; transform and key edits still support undo/redo. Save/Open includes all joints and their animation. Authored and imported joints support transform keys. Use Skinning to bind or rebind meshes; inverse kinematics is not implemented. Joint safety limits: 512 joints, position/rotation components within ±1,000,000 (radians internally), scale within ±100.

        IMPORT, ENTIRELY OFFLINE

        Select a GLB, or a GLTF together with its buffers and images. Import a folder to preserve texture paths. Multiple models retain their authored coordinates. Each file shows its active scene; selecting a node in another scene switches that model’s scene. Source node names and child order are preserved, including duplicates. Multi-primitive meshes have additional primitive rows. Removing a model releases its resources and its authored animation tracks.

        PRIVATE BY DESIGN

        Three.js r160 is embedded in this file. GLTFLoader, Draco, Meshopt and Basis/KTX2 decoders are also embedded. No remote requests, accounts or uploads. Local blob URLs are used only to decode files and start workers.
